notes.meaning: Isaiah pauses to praise God directly, calling Him his own God. He worships the Lord for carrying out the wonderful plans He made long ago in perfect faithfulness. Everything God does is steady, true, and completely reliable.

God tears down proud, fortified cities that set themselves up against Him, turning them into piles of stone that will never be rebuilt. While this pointed to historic oppressors like Babylon or Nineveh, it also pictures every worldly power that opposes God's people. No earthly fortress can stand when the Lord decides to bring it down.

When fierce and powerful nations witness God's righteous judgments, they are struck with holy awe. Instead of boasting in their own might, ruthless peoples learn to revere and honor the true God. The fall of human pride leads the world to acknowledge the Lord's supreme authority.

God is a safe haven for poor and needy believers when cruel enemies attack them. The blast of ruthless oppressors is like a rainstorm beating against a sturdy stone wall, or baking heat in a desert. Just as a thick cloud cools down scorching sunlight, God steps in and silences the shouting of His enemies.

On Mount Zion, which represents God's presence and His church, the Lord prepares a rich banquet for people from every nation. This magnificent feast of choice food and fine wine pictures the spiritual joy, peace, and rich blessings offered freely in the gospel. Both Jews and Gentiles are welcomed to sit down together at God's table.

differ.view: Reformed teachers see this feast as the spiritual blessings and comforts of the gospel enjoyed in the church.
Some evangelicals understand this banquet as a literal earthly feast celebrating Christ's final victory.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The banquet of rich food and wine promised on God's holy mountain is seen as fulfilled in the celebration of the Mass.

notes.meaning: God promises to destroy the dark covering that hangs over all the nations of the earth. This veil pictures spiritual blindness and ignorance of the true God, as well as the dark shroud of grief worn by mourners. The Lord removes this shadow so people everywhere can see His truth and light.

The Lord will swallow up death forever, defeating it completely through the resurrection of Christ. He will gently wipe away every tear of sorrow from the faces of His people and remove their earthly disgrace. Because the Lord has spoken, this final victory over grief and death is absolutely certain.

When God's great rescue arrives, His people will rejoice together that their quiet trust was rewarded. They will gladly say that this is the very God they have waited for, and He has truly delivered them. Waiting on the Lord is never wasted, because His salvation brings everlasting joy.

The protective hand of the Lord will rest permanently over His holy mountain to bless His church. At the same time, Moab—representing all proud enemies who oppose God—will be trampled down into ruin like straw crushed into manure. God preserves His people while bringing total defeat upon those who resist Him.

The proud oppressor will thrash and struggle in vain under God's judgment, like someone desperately flailing their arms to stay afloat. Despite all their cleverness and hard effort, they cannot rescue themselves. The Lord will bring their boastful pride down into utter defeat.

Even the highest walls and strongest towers of the enemy will be pulled down by God's power. Those mighty fortresses will be leveled flat and scattered into common dust. No human defense can protect the wicked when God carries out His righteous judgment.
